diagrams.title: **Called vs listening
diagrams.caption: **Called vs listening.** The model client and any expensive setup are created once when the container starts and live for the life of the container.
diagrams.svg:

diagrams.title: **Browser → load balancer → container → model and tools
diagrams.caption: **Browser → load balancer → container → model and tools.** The load balancer is the front door; the ECS service keeps the containers behind it alive.
diagrams.svg:

The agent calls Amazon Bedrock for reasoning and its tools: an EHR system for patient and procedure data, a calendar API for provider availability, and an SMS service for appointment confirmations. diagrams.title: **Recipe, kitchen, dishes
diagrams.caption: **Recipe, kitchen, dishes.** The task definition describes one container; the service keeps the right number of them running inside a cluster.
diagrams.svg:

Below, two ways to supply the compute: Fargate, where you specify CPU and memory and AWS handles the servers, recommended to start; or the EC2 launch type, where you manage the instances yourself, for needs like GPUs." style="max-width:100%;height:auto;display:block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><defs><marker id="ah" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5" markerWidth="7" markerHeight="7" orient="auto-start-reverse"><path class="ah" d="M0,0 L10,5 L0,10 z"></path></marker></defs>

      <text x="40" y="54" class="t" style="font-family:'Plus Jakarta Sans', sans-serif;fill:#19203F;font-size:19px;font-weight:700">Task definition</text><text x="40" y="78" class="ts" style="font-family:'Plus Jakarta Sans', sans-serif;fill:#586082;font-size:16px;font-weight:400">the recipe card</text>

      <text x="40" y="224" class="tm" style="font-family:'Plus Jakarta Sans', sans-serif;fill:#3A4266;font-size:16px">• logs → CloudWatch</text>
      <path d="M324 135 H376" class="ln" stroke-width="3" marker-end="url(#ah)" style="stroke:#3A4266;stroke-width:2.5;fill:none"></path>

diagrams.title: **Seven steps, all visible in one script
diagrams.caption: **Seven steps, all visible in one script.** Every `aws` command in `deploy.sh` is something a platform team would otherwise do in the console.
diagrams.svg:
<svg viewBox="0 0 1100 430" class="dimmable" aria-label="The seven steps of the ECS deploy script. Step 1 creates an ECR repository. Step 2 builds the Docker image on your machine and pushes it to ECR. Step 3 creates two IAM roles: an execution role that lets ECS pull the image and write logs, and a task role that lets your agent call Bedrock. Step 4 creates the ECS cluster. Step 5 creates a CloudWatch log group. Step 6 registers the task definition. Step 7 creates the load balancer, target group, security groups and the Fargate service, which starts the task." style="max-width:100%;height:auto;display:block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><defs><marker id="ah" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5" markerWidth="7" markerHeight="7" orient="auto-start-reverse"><path class="ah" d="M0,0 L10,5 L0,10 z"></path></marker><marker id="ah-data" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5" markerWidth="7" markerHeight="7" orient="auto-start-reverse"><path class="ah-data" d="M0,0 L10,5 L0,10 z"></path></marker></defs>

diagrams.caption: **Two locked doors.** Only you can reach the load balancer, and only the load balancer can reach the container.

diagrams.title: **Teams in one box, and setup paid once
diagrams.caption: **Teams in one box, and setup paid once.** These are the two situations where an always-on container clearly beats a function.

diagrams.title: **The part nobody warns you about
diagrams.caption: **The part nobody warns you about.** Generic infrastructure is well understood; the agent-specific layer on top is where teams lose weeks.
diagrams.svg:
<svg viewBox="0 0 1100 330" aria-label="Two layers of production work. The bottom layer is generic infrastructure, the same for any web app: containers, load balancers, IAM roles, health checks, scaling, certificates and VPC networking. The top layer is agent-specific and generic compute doesn't provide it: per-user session isolation so one conversation can't leak into another, tool-level authorisation so an agent can't exceed its boundaries, identity propagation so tools act on behalf of the right user, and observability of reasoning steps rather than just HTTP error codes. On Lambda or ECS you build the top layer yourself." style="max-width:100%;height:auto;display:block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
      <rect x="20" y="20" width="1060" height="170" rx="20" class="bx2" style="fill:#F8F9FC;stroke:#C4344F;stroke-width:2.5"></rect>

diagrams.title: **The user sees a report with charts
diagrams.caption: **The user sees a report with charts.** Behind it, the AgentCore stack coordinates securely, with governance and full traceability. On Lambda or ECS you'd build most of this coordination yourself.
